That's very likely the real cause — **"Data Disabled" means your phone's mobile data switch is OFF**, and MMS (picture messaging) requires an active mobile data connection, even when you have full 5G signal. Refueling the data fixed the account-side limit, but your phone still won't route MMS while the data switch is off.

Here's what I'd like you to do next, on the phone itself:

**1. Turn mobile data back ON**
- Open **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network** (on many phones: **Settings → Connections → Mobile networks**), and switch **Mobile data** to ON.
- Quick alternative: swipe down from the top of the screen to open the quick settings panel and tap the **Mobile data / Data** tile so it's enabled.

**2. Confirm it worked**
- Your status bar should now show the network indicator (e.g. 5G/LTE) **without** "Data Disabled".
- Then try sending one picture message again.

**3. While you're in Settings, one quick check**
- Make sure **Airplane Mode** is OFF (a reboot sometimes leaves it on), and check that **Data Saver** is OFF, since it can also block MMS.

Please try that and let me know what the status bar shows afterward. If the picture message still fails once data is confirmed ON, tell me and we'll move on to checking your APN/MMSC settings — that's the next most common cause of MMS-only failures.

Yes — with data confirmed ON and you still having 5G signal, the next most likely cause is your **APN settings**, specifically the **MMSC URL** (the server address that handles picture messages). Regular SMS works without it, which matches exactly what you're seeing.

Here's what I'd like you to check and do on the phone:

**1. Check your current APN settings**
- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → Advanced → Access Point Names (APN)**.
- Look at the **MMSC** field (and the **APN** field itself).
- If the MMSC field is blank, or the APN shows as incorrect, that's our culprit.

**2. If it's blank/incorrect, reset to default**
- Tap the **three-dot menu (⋮)** in the top-right corner and choose **Reset to default**.
- Then make sure the correct APN entry is selected (it will have a dot/ radio button next to it).

**3. Reboot the phone**
- This step is important — the new APN/MMSC settings won't take effect until the phone restarts.

**4. Test again**
- After the reboot, confirm your status bar shows 5G with data enabled, then try sending the picture message.

Let me know what the APN/MMSC screen shows — and tell me whether the MMSC field was empty or already filled in. turns.thought:
Thanks for sticking with it — and good news on one front: the MMSC field being empty **was** a real problem, so that reset was a necessary fix (your picture messages could not have worked without an MMSC URL). It's just that there appears to be more than one thing going on. Since we've now confirmed signal, data, and APN are all good, let's move to the next two items.

**1. Turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF (most likely remaining cause)**
Wi-Fi Calling can conflict with MMS on some configurations, especially when your carrier handles MMS over the cellular data path.
- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Calls & SMS → Wi-Fi Calling** (on some phones: **Settings → Connections → Wi-Fi Calling**, or search "Wi-Fi Calling" in Settings).
- Check whether it's ON. **If it is, switch it OFF.**
- Wait a few seconds, then try sending your picture message again **without rebooting**.

**2. If that doesn't work — check your messaging app permissions**
The app needs both **Storage** (to attach the picture) and **SMS** (to send it). A recent app or OS update can quietly revoke these.
- Go to **Settings → Apps → See all apps → Messages** (your messaging app) → **Permissions**.
- Confirm **Storage / Photos and videos** is set to **Allow**, and **SMS** is set to **Allow**.
- If either says "Denied" or "Ask every time," set it to **Allow**.
- Then try the picture message again.

Try Wi-Fi Calling first, then permissions, and let me know the result of each. If picture messages still fail after both, I'll escalate you to a human agent with a full summary of everything we've already ruled out — you won't have to start over from scratch, and I'll tell you that before I do it.

Also, one small note for your records: the 2 GB data refuel I added remains valid and usable through the end of your cycle (2025-02-28), so that $4.00 wasn't wasted regardless of the MMS outcome — it also covers your regular browsing.
